title: Finite finitely presented pushforward preserves constructible etale modules
statement: Let $X,Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. If $F$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], then the direct image $f_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$.

source.place: Tag 095R, label lemma-finite-pushforward-constructible, finite-ring and qcqs specialization

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-quasicompact-affine-surjection], choose a surjection a₀ : Spec R → Y. Base change f along a₀, with projections b₀ : X₀ → X and f₀ : X₀ → Spec R. The map f₀ is finite and locally of finite presentation by base change [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and X₀ is affine. The inverse image b₀^*F is constructible by [prop-constructible-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]. Finite exchange [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] identifies a₀^*(f_*F) with f₀_*b₀^*F. Therefore constructibility for finite finitely presented morphisms of affine schemes implies the original assertion by isomorphism invariance [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance] and surjective descent [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-surjective-descent]. All schemes to which descent is applied are qcqs: Y by hypothesis and Spec R by affineness. No flatness is needed. Work henceforth with X,Y affine.

source.place: Tag 095R affine reduction, implemented via Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiCompact.compactSpace_iff_exists and the same finite exchange and surjective descent as the next reduction.

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-finite-qf], $f$ is quasi-finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasifinite-affine-etale-thickening-decomposition] to obtain a surjection $a:Y\prime\to Y$ with $Y\prime$ affine, $X\prime=X\times_Y Y\prime$, projection $b:X\prime\to X$, and a surjective closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X\prime$ such that $e=f\prime\circ i:Z\to Y\prime$ is finite etale. The base change $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$ is finite, and $X\prime$ is affine, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Also $Z$ is affine, being closed in $X\prime$; thus $X\prime,Y\prime,Z$ are qcqs. No flatness of $a$ is assumed or used.

Put $F\prime=b^{-1}F$. By [prop-constructible-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison], $F\prime$ and then $H=i^{-1}F\prime$ are constructible module sheaves. These pullbacks have the same constant coefficient ring $\Lambda$, by [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. All three schemes here are qcqs and $\Lambda$ is finite, so the comparison applies without changing the coefficient category or the finiteness condition.

The thickening $i$ induces an equivalence of small etale sites by [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site]. This equivalence also identifies the categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules: it carries the constant ring to the constant ring and preserves finite products. Explicitly a module object has zero $1\to F$, addition $F\times F\to F$, and action $\Lambda\times F\to F$ satisfying the module identities. Applying either functor of the equivalence to these maps, with its product and constant-ring identifications, gives these same identities on the image. The unit and counit commute with each of these maps by naturality, so they are module-linear. Its pullback and right adjoint direct image are quasi-inverses, hence the adjunction unit is an isomorphism $F\prime\simeq i_*H$. Consequently $f\prime_*F\prime\simeq e_*H$. For clarity, the latter composition identification is the module-linear sectionwise identification $H((W\times_{Y\prime}X\prime)\times_{X\prime}Z)=H(W\times_{Y\prime}Z)$, natural in $W$, using the direct-image formula. This is a topos equivalence argument, not a claim that constructibility alone implies $F\prime=i_*i^{-1}F\prime$.

source.place: 095R parenthesis: thickening induces an equivalence of etale topoi; 03SI (theorem-topological-invariance)

proof.text: Since $e$ is finite etale and $H$ is constructible, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-pushforward-constructible] gives constructibility of $e_*H$. The isomorphism in Step 4 therefore makes $f\prime_*F\prime$ constructible. Isomorphism invariance is [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance], applied through [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] to the module category; all schemes used here are qcqs.

Finite exchange [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] in the cartesian square for $a$ identifies $a^{-1}(f_*F)$ with $f\prime_*b^{-1}F=f\prime_*F\prime$. Thus $a^{-1}(f_*F)$ is constructible, by [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance] for $\mathrm{ModuleCat}(\Lambda)$-valued sheaves, and the two directions of [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-surjective-descent] to $a:Y\prime\to Y$: it is surjective and both schemes are affine, hence qcqs. This proves constructibility of $f_*F$ in the affine case, and the affine-surjection reduction of Step 1 proves it on the original qcqs $Y$.
